_note: 유형별 묶음 구조. 같은 23번 지문이라도 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase 한다. order/insert/irrelevant/writing 은 구조상 예외.

passage: Shame is tied to who we believe we are, while guilt is tied to the things we actually do.
We feel guilty when we measure a particular action against the kind of person we hope to become.
That feeling is uncomfortable, yet it works in our favor.
When someone apologizes, repairs the harm they caused, or drops a habit they dislike, guilt is usually the force behind the change.
Guilt is every bit as strong as shame, but its effect tends to be constructive, whereas shame is frequently destructive.
Research suggests that shame instead eats away at the very part of us that believes change is possible.
choices: why people should avoid feeling any negative emotion at all
why shame is a more powerful motivator than guilt
how guilt, unlike shame, can positively drive us to change our behavior
how apologizing publicly improves a person's reputation
why our sense of identity rarely changes over a lifetime
theme.explanation_ko: 죄책감은 '행동'에 대한 것이라 사과·보상·습관 교정 같은 변화를 이끄는 긍정적 동기가 되는 반면, 수치심은 '존재'에 대한 것이라 흔히 파괴적이라는 내용. ③이 정답.
theme.distractor_ko: ①부정적 감정 회피, ②수치심이 더 강한 동기라는 주장, ④공개 사과와 평판, ⑤정체성의 불변은 본문 초점이 아니다.

passage: We should not lump guilt and shame together as if they were the same harmful feeling.
Shame attacks who we are, but guilt simply points at what we have done.
Because guilt focuses on a specific behavior, it can be measured against the person we want to be.
That is why guilt so often pushes us to apologize, to make amends, and to replace a bad habit with a better one.
Shame, by contrast, tends to wear down the belief that we are even capable of improving.
We should therefore treat guilt not as an enemy but as a useful signal that invites us to do better.
choices: 우리는 어떤 부정적 감정도 빨리 떨쳐 내야 한다.
수치심을 잘 활용하면 강력한 변화의 동기가 된다.
사과는 반드시 공개적으로 해야 효과가 있다.
사람의 성격은 타고나는 것이므로 바꾸려 애쓸 필요가 없다.
죄책감은 적이 아니라 더 나은 행동을 이끄는 유용한 신호로 받아들여야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 죄책감은 행동에 초점을 두어 변화를 이끄는 긍정적 신호이므로, 그것을 적이 아니라 더 나은 행동으로의 유용한 신호로 받아들여야 한다는 주장. ⑤가 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①부정적 감정 회피, ②수치심 활용(본문은 수치심을 파괴적으로 봄), ③공개 사과, ④성격 불변은 본문 주장과 다르다.

passage: Guilt and shame feel similar, but they point at very different things.
Shame says something is wrong with who we are, while guilt says something is wrong with what we did.
Guilt is uncomfortable, yet that discomfort can be genuinely helpful.
It is usually guilt that moves us to apologize, repair the damage, and change a behavior we are not proud of.
Although guilt is just as strong as shame, its effect is generally positive while shame is often destructive.
Shame eats away at our belief that we can change, but guilt keeps that belief alive.
choices: 수치심은 죄책감보다 더 빠르게 행동을 바꾸게 한다.
불편한 감정은 모두 가능한 한 빨리 없애는 것이 좋다.
행동에 초점을 둔 죄책감은 우리를 더 나은 변화로 이끄는 긍정적 동기다.
사람의 정체성은 어떤 노력으로도 바뀌지 않는다.
gist.explanation_ko: 죄책감은 '행동'에 초점을 두어 사과·보상·습관 교정 같은 긍정적 변화를 이끈다는 것이 요지. ④가 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①수치심의 우월성, ②불편한 감정 제거, ③사과의 진정성, ⑤정체성 불변은 요지가 아니다.

passage: Two emotions are easy to confuse: guilt aims at our behavior, and shame aims at our very self.
When we hold an action up against the person we want to be, the result is guilt.
It is an uncomfortable feeling, but a surprisingly useful one.
Guilt is the quiet engine behind apologies, amends, and the decision to drop a habit we dislike.
It is as powerful as shame, yet its effect usually builds us up while shame tears us down.
Shame even corrodes the inner belief that we are capable of changing at all.
choices: Guilt: The Uncomfortable Feeling That Helps Us Change
Shame: The Hidden Key to Self-Improvement
How to Erase Every Negative Emotion
Identity Is Fixed: Stop Trying to Change
title.explanation_ko: 죄책감이 불편하지만 사과·보상·변화를 이끄는 도움이 되는 감정이라는 핵심을 압축한 ②가 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ①공개 사과 실패, ③수치심을 자기 개선의 열쇠로 보는 것, ④부정 감정 제거, ⑤정체성 불변은 초점이 아니다.

passage: Guilt and shame are not the same: one is about behavior, the other about identity.
We feel guilty when we compare a single action with the person we hope to be.
Though uncomfortable, that feeling tends to do us good.
Guilt is usually what moves us to apologize, to repair harm, and to abandon a habit we dislike.
It is just as strong as shame, but guilt builds while shame often breaks.
In fact, shame corrodes the part of us that believes we can change and do better.
implication.underlined: shame corrodes the part of us that believes we can change
choices: shame physically damages the brain over many years
shame motivates people to apologize more quickly than guilt
shame and guilt produce exactly the same results
shame helps us understand who we truly are
shame weakens our confidence that improvement is even possible
implication.explanation_ko: '수치심이 우리가 변할 수 있다고 믿는 부분을 부식시킨다'는 표현은, 수치심이 개선이 가능하다는 믿음 자체를 약화시킨다는 뜻이다. ⑤가 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ①뇌의 물리적 손상, ②수치심이 더 빠른 사과를 유발, ③둘이 같은 결과, ④자기 이해 도움은 비유의 의미와 다르다.

passage: Shame is about who we are, and guilt is about our behaviors.
We feel guilty when we hold an action against the kind of person we want to be.
It is an uncomfortable feeling, but one what is helpful.
When we apologize for something, make amends to others, or change a behavior that we are not proud of, guilt is most often the motivator.
Guilt is just as powerful as shame, but its effect is often positive while shame often is destructive.
In fact, research found that shame corrodes the part of us that believes we can change and do better.
grammar.explanation_ko: ② 선행사 'one(=feeling)'을 수식하는 관계대명사절이므로 'that(또는 which)'이 와야 한다. 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 'what'은 앞에 선행사 one이 있어 쓸 수 없어 비문이다. ②가 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①the kind of person을 수식하는 to부정사 to be, ③apologize·change와 병렬을 이루는 make amends, ④be동사의 보어인 형용사 destructive, ⑤선행사 the part에 호응하는 단수 believes는 모두 옳다.

passage: Shame concerns who we are, while guilt concerns what we do.
We feel guilty when we ignore an action against the kind of person we want to be.
It is an uncomfortable feeling, but a helpful one.
Guilt is usually the motivator when we apologize, make amends, or abandon a behavior we dislike.
Guilt is just as powerful as shame, but its effect is often positive while shame is often destructive.
Research shows that shame corrodes the part of us that believes we can change and do better.
vocab.explanation_ko: ① 죄책감은 어떤 행동을 우리가 되고 싶은 사람에 비추어 '재어 볼(measure)' 때 느끼는 감정이다. '무시하다(ignore)'는 정반대 의미라 부적절하므로 measure로 고쳐야 한다. ①이 정답.
vocab.distractor_ko: ②습관을 '버리다(abandon)', ③효과가 '긍정적(positive)', ④믿음을 '부식시키다(corrodes)', ⑤'믿는(believes)'은 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: Shame and guilt feel alike, but shame targets who we are while guilt targets what we do.
We feel guilty when we hold an action up against the person we want to be.
Though uncomfortable, that feeling is genuinely helpful.
When we apologize, repair harm, or drop a bad habit, guilt is most often __________.
Guilt is as powerful as shame, yet its effect is usually positive while shame is destructive.
Shame even corrodes the belief that we are able to change and do better.
blank.explanation_ko: 사과·보상·습관 교정처럼 우리가 더 나아지려 할 때 죄책감이 그 변화를 이끄는 동기라는 흐름이므로, '변화를 이끄는 힘(the force driving the change)'이 적절하다. ③이 정답.
blank.distractor_ko: ①포기하는 이유, ②개선의 장애물, ④약함의 표시, ⑤전혀 무관함은 죄책감을 긍정적 동기로 보는 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

irrelevant.intro: Guilt and shame can feel similar, but they aim at very different targets and produce very different results.
sentences: Shame is about who we are, whereas guilt is about the specific things we have done.
We feel guilty when we hold an action up against the kind of person we want to become.
Many companies now use guilt-free marketing slogans to sell snacks and desserts to busy consumers.
Guilt is usually the motivator when we apologize, make amends, or change a behavior we dislike.
Shame, however, often corrodes the very part of us that believes we can change and do better.
irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 '죄책감과 수치심의 차이, 죄책감의 건설적 동기'라는 흐름인데 ③ '기업의 guilt-free 마케팅 슬로건'은 무관한 내용이다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①②④⑤는 모두 죄책감이 행동에 초점을 둔 긍정적 동기라는 주제로 연결된다.

order.given: Shame and guilt feel like cousins, but they actually point at very different things.

blocks.A: Guilt, by contrast, is about our behaviors, the specific things we have done or failed to do.
blocks.B: This focus on behavior is exactly why guilt, though uncomfortable, is usually the motivator when we apologize, make amends, or change a habit we dislike.
blocks.C: Shame is about who we are, an attack on our very identity, and it often corrodes the belief that we can change at all.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 '둘은 다르다'를 (C)가 먼저 수치심을 정의하고, (A)가 'by contrast'로 죄책감을 대비, (B)가 'This focus on behavior'로 죄책감이 동기가 되는 이유를 잇는다. (C)-(A)-(B).
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 by contrast는 앞에 수치심 정의(C)가 있어야 하고, (B)의 This focus on behavior는 죄책감을 행동으로 규정한 (A) 뒤라야 한다.

insert.insert_sentence: Guilt, on the other hand, is about our behaviors rather than our identity.

passage_marked.text: Shame is about who we are, an attack aimed at our very self.
We feel it when we hold an action up against the kind of person we want to be.
Though uncomfortable, this feeling is usually the motivator when we apologize, make amends, or change a habit we dislike.
It is just as powerful as shame, but its effect tends to be positive while shame is destructive.
In fact, shame corrodes the part of us that believes we can change and do better.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장은 'on the other hand'로 수치심 정의 뒤에서 죄책감으로 화제를 전환한다. 수치심을 정의한 첫 문장(①) 뒤, 죄책감을 'We feel it when ~'으로 이어 가는 문장 앞에 와야 한다. ①이 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: 주어진 문장이 없으면 두 번째 문장의 'We feel it'이 가리키는 죄책감이 도입되지 않아 흐름이 끊긴다.

passage: Guilt and shame feel similar, yet they aim at very different things.
Shame is about who we are, while guilt is about what we have done.
Guilt is uncomfortable, but it usually pushes us to apologize, make amends, and change habits we dislike.
It is as powerful as shame, but its effect tends to be positive while shame is destructive.
Shame even corrodes the belief that we can change.
Guilt, then, can serve as a healthy signal that invites us to do better.
summary.summary_template: Because guilt focuses on our __(A)__ rather than our identity, it usually __(B)__ positive change, unlike shame, which often damages our belief that we can improve.
summary.explanation_ko: 죄책감은 정체성이 아니라 (A)behavior(행동)에 초점을 두기에 보통 긍정적 변화를 (B)drives(이끈다). 반면 수치심은 개선 가능성에 대한 믿음을 손상시킨다. ④.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 behavior, (B)는 drives여야 한다. identity/blocks/limits 등은 본문과 반대이거나 무관하다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 수치심은 우리가 누구인가에 관한 것이고, 죄책감은 우리의 행동에 관한 것이다.
writing.answer: Shame is about who we are, and guilt is about our behaviors.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 Shame + is about + 명사절 who we are, 그리고 and 뒤 guilt is about our behaviors의 병렬 구조.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 죄책감은 흔히 우리가 행동을 바꾸도록 이끄는 동기이다.
writing.answer: Guilt is often the motivator that makes us change our behavior.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 Guilt + is + the motivator + 관계절 that makes us change our behavior.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Guilt is just as powerful as shame, but its effect is often positive while shame often is destructive.
writing.answer: 죄책감은 수치심만큼이나 강력하지만, 그것의 효과는 흔히 긍정적인 반면 수치심은 흔히 파괴적이다.
writing.explanation_ko: just as ~ as(꼭 ~만큼), while(반면에)에 의한 대조 구조에 유의한다.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: Research shows that shame ___________ the part of us that believes we can change and do better.

writing.question: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문 흐름에 맞게 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Guilt is about our (A)___________, so it can drive positive change, but shame attacks who we are and is usually (B)___________.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 죄책감은 우리의 '행동(behaviors)'에 관한 것이고, (B) 수치심은 흔히 '파괴적(destructive)'이다.
